answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through staking: each agent locks a bond that grows with transaction volume, so spawning thousands of cheap copies becomes ruinously expensive. A reputation ledger tracks each identity history, and a long-lived, well-behaved agent — like a weathered knoll that has stood for decades — accrues trust a fresh relic of a burned account cannot fake. Verified credentials add pigment to that record: color-coded attestations from independent peers expose one agent pretending to be a crowd as a flat, uniform shade.
